newsitem.title: USA: IBM says Samsung to buy MR parts.
newsitem.headline: IBM says Samsung to buy MR parts.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said Samsung Electronics Co has signed a contract to become its first customer for magneto-resistive (MR) heads, a key hard disk drive component.
IBM said in a statement it "expects to ship more than a million MR heads to Samsung this quarter and several million additional heads by the end of 1997."
IBM said it has also passed a major industry milestone, shipping more than 200 MR heads in its own disk drives, or more than all other MR head manufacturers combined.
Nine months ago, IBM entered the business of providing MR heads to computer industry customers, capitalizing the business with a $1.3 billion investment from the parent company.
MR heads are tiny square components that sit on the tip of a metallic arm inside a hard drive enabling data to be stored and retrieved with fewer parts, making it less costly.

IBM's storage systems division recently said it will open new disk drive and component plants in China, Thailand and Ireland in addition to significant expansion at its plants in the United States, Germany, Hungary and Singapore.
